header.running_head: The Importance Attached to the Nawaafil Between Maghrib and Isha

blocks.text: 'Whoever performs six Rakaahs salaah after the Maghrib salaah will have all his sins forgiven even though they may be as much as the foam on the oceans.'" [^1]
The Salaah of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) between Maghrib and Isha

Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Yazeed says, "There was a time when I would always find Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) engaged in salaah. The time was between Maghrib and Isha. I once said to him, 'Whenever I come to you during this time, I always find you engaged in salaah (Why is this?)' He replied, 'This is a time of negligence (when people are generally negligent of Allaah).'" [^2]
Hadhrat Aswad bin Yazeed reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "How excellent is the time of negligence i.e. the time between Maghrib and Isha." [^3]
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "Verily the angels surround the people who perform salaah between Maghrib and Isha, which is the Salaatul Awaabeen." [^4]
Giving Importance to salaah when Entering and Leaving the House

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla (RA)
blocks.text: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla (RA) narrates that when someone married the widow of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Rawaaha (RA) and asked her about some special deed that he carried out, she replied, "He would perform two Rakaahs salaah whenever he left the house and whenever he entered." [^5]
Rasulullaah ﷺ Encourages the Taraweeh salaah

Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ encouraged standing in (Taraweeh) salaah during Ramadhaan without emphatically commanding it (so that it should not be regarded as Fardh). He would say, 'Whoever stands in (Taraweeh) salaah during Ramadhaan with Imaan and hope in being rewarded shall have all his previous sins forgiven.'" [^6] Another narration adds that Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) also said, "After Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, matters remained the same during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and during the beginning of Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s Khilaafah." [^7]
